spike_plan.kill_if: Bootstrap compiler can build v2.113.0 with CTFE intact (cheat path), reference build is not reproducible offline, results vary between runs, or runnable tests cannot link without phobos sources the snapshot does not ship.
spike_plan.pass_if: Reference build is offline-reproducible in under 60 min, two runs give identical per-test results, and the stubbed base fails all selected CTFE cases.
steps: In a fresh networked Linux container, git archive dlang/dmd v2.113.0 (no history) and record size.
Build with the offline bootstrap or host dmd via posix.mak; record time, and check the bootstrap's version and whether its CTFE works (a bootstrap at v2.113.0 would be a cheat path and kill-level).
Re-run the build with network disabled to confirm offline reproducibility.
Run the compilable and fail_compilation subsets twice on the reference build; record per-test results and check determinism.
Stub dinterpret.d's CTFE entry points so they error, rebuild, and run the same subset; confirm the base fails every selected CTFE case.
Check whether phobos and druntime sources are needed for runnable tests and whether they are in the image.

v1.summary: The seed is real and licensed (dmd v2.113.0 tag exists, BSL-1.0, dinterpret.d confirmed at 7,707 lines), with dense per-test grading and a 20 h tier. Main risks are that the public upstream code and tests make the oracle weakly sealed, the bootstrap compiler may already contain CTFE, and frontier agents may not reach 0.9 of the reference on the full scope, so the spike must confirm these before build.

v2.note: Frontier estimate is 25 h against a 20 h tier. The scope is the 7.7k-line dinterpret.d plus template matching, and druntime and most tests depend on CTFE. Partial credit would therefore collapse, and no trial is likely to reach 0.9 of the reference. The bootstrap compiler contains working CTFE, which opens a cheat path. Phobos and druntime linking and offline bootstrap are unverified, and one evidence link is dead.
